recipes.name: Delicious Apple Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 2 (8 ounce) packages refrigerated crescent roll dough
4 small Granny Smith apple, peeled, cored, and quartered
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle caffeinated citrus-flavored soda (such as Mountain Dew®)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Heat sugar, butter, cinnamon, and vanilla in a saucepan over medium heat until sugar dissolves, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat; set aside.
Divide crescent roll dough into 16 triangles. Roll 1 apple quarter with 1 dough triangle; arrange in the prepared pan. Pour butter mixture over wrapped apples; pour soda on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 40 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Apple Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: This delicious apple dumplings recipe is made with green apples, wrapped in crescent roll dough, baked with a buttery, combo of citrus soda and cinnamon.

review.reviewBody: Wow - What a fabulous recipe! I mean a dessert just doesn't get any easier or any tastier than this! Definitely not for those counting calories...although I'm sure it could be lightened up a bit if you wanted to! I used half white sugar and half brown sugar, added 1/4 tsp. of nutmeg. I also had to sub Sprite for the Mountain Dew as I didn't have any on hand. These baked up beautifully and made the house smell wonderful. They were perfect with vanilla ice cream and a dollup of whipped cream and the side -YUM!

I LOVE these dumplings. They are so quick and easy to make, and as others posted, make the home smell wonderful. I got this recipe from my cousin except there were a few differences.
2 sticks of butter. Melt butter, sugar, and vanilla. 2 large apples instead of 4 small ones. Spray pan instead of greasing it. I used 1 Granny Smith Apple and 1 Pink Lady Apple. I've used Sprite and 7-Up. Either one is OK to use. I sprinkled a little brown sugar and nutmeg over the prepared dumplings. Next time, I will add the brown sugar and nutmeg to the sugar, butter and vanilla while it's cooking.
Another reviewer said her dumplings were hard to remove from the pan if you didn't remove them right away after baking. I've made them twice in the past 2 weeks, once for home, and once for work (E-mailing the recipe to co-workers now.), and I didn't have a problem with them sticking to the pan. Of course, my pan was sprayed, and it was glass.

These were very good! I used 1/2 white sugar 1/2 brown sugar. I also tossed the cut up apples in cinnamon and sugar and added some nutmeg like suggested by another review. I also added the soda around the pan and not on top. I will definitely make these again.

Great recipe! I changed a few things just from making it a few times. -not a change, but keep the Granny Smith apples! You need that tartness /sourness to balance out the sweet. -instead of 1 cup of white sugar, I did about a little over 1/3 of a cup of brown sugar and a little over 1/3 cup of white sugar. Slightly less sugar, but you won’t notice and the brown sugar flavor is so needed! -pour the Mountain Dew around the dumplings and not on. —I made the change of following the max cook time instead of the minimum and it was worth it. My husband was the one to mention it when he said they were the perfect texture this time (less soggy, more crispy on top)

Easy to make and everyone loved them! I used half white and half brown sugar as suggested by others and tossed the apple pieces with a bit of the sugar and cinnamon mixture before wrapping them in the dough. Also added a pinch of nutmeg. Served with vanilla ice cream. I also cut up two extra apples, tossed in the sugar mixture and placed them in the dish to cook with the dumplings. It was really good!

I have made this many times and everyone loves it. I tweaked it just a bit by sprinkling cinnamon on the apples before I roll it up in the dough and also using some brown sugar too. I also drizzle caramel syrup over dumplings as soon as they come out of the oven and then yes definitely serve with ice cream.

I found this recipe somewhere else originally and though it sounded weird, tried it with fresh plums and diet lemon lime soda. I only made a half a batch with one can of crescent rolls. The two of us practically finished the entire pan! I also baked it on convection mode. And a dollop of sour cream on top, cut the sweetness and was a nice addition. OK, I was out of ice cream - drat!

I've been making this recipe since I first learned when I was a kid. I always use brown sugar and I wisk in the cinnamon and a little nutmeg in with the brown sugar. This is really awesome with cinnamon ice cream or fresh whipped cream. GREAT white trash party offering. EDITED REVIEW: I made this the other day using reduced fat crescent roll, half the amount of butter, half the amount of brown sugar Splenda in place of the sugar and Diet Canada Dry. Even using the lower fat ingredients, this was still freaking awesome. I ate one portion, the boys literally ate the rest in 15 minutes. My husband even remarked that it's better than it usually is!

This is an amazing dessert. I do not cook the sugar mixture & use 2 large apples. Also I use lower fat crescent rolls, Splenda for the sugar & sugar-free Mountain Dew. No one can tell the difference. I get requests to bring this to potluck all the time.

Very simple and easy to make. I am not certain if I didn't read the reviews in their entirety but didn't know this: REMOVE DUMPLINGS FROM PAN WHILE HOT AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER TAKING OUT OF THE OVEN. Once cooled, the sugar and soda caramelizes and it is extremely difficult to remove dumplings. Also, add sugar and cinnamon to apples too for added flavor. I paired this with butter pecan ice cream and my significant other loved it. Will make again for those I love!

OMG, so good!! I took some advice from others and sprinkled cinnamon and brown sugar on the apples before wrapping them, used diet Mt. Dew and only used about 1/2 cup of it. DEEELISH! Even had the kids help make them and they loved it. I also used the grand size cresent rolls and just cut them in half instead of using 2 full cans. Will definitely keep this recipe! Thanks for sharing!
This was so easy to make and tasted sooo good. Will definitely be making this again!!!
My family loves this

Super Easy & it tastes great And it is so beautiful it looks like I spent a long time preparing it when I didn’t! Love it! I didn’t have enough apples so I wrapped the last 4 with coconut pressed into the dough put them on the sides of dumplings & I love them to!
Super easy, super delicious, & I used 1 1/2c sugar & lined the pan with foil for easy cleanup. Also keep Amaretto in the house. If you run out of vanilla, it’s a Great substitute!
So easy and delicious with a scoop of vanilla ice cream!

I followed the recipe almost exactly. It came out perfect. I used three apples instead of four, but using an apple corer I was able to have plenty of apple for each crescent roll. I used the exact amount of sugar , butter and vanilla. and I used a bottle of squirt. It was perfect. The very top of the dumpling gets a nice little crunch to it and the inside is a nice tender apple with just the perfect kind of sweetness. I did Think that maybe next time I might sprinkle some turbinado sugar on top to give it a little more of a sweet crunch but you absolutely don’t have to do anything to this other than maybe next time have some vanilla ice cream or whipped cream on hand.
This was such a huge hit in my family. Made it for extended family as well and they LOVED it. My husband said it was better than apple pie, but do NOT serve without ice cream.
We make it all the time. Cooks best in convection toaster-oven.

Very tasty. I forgot the vanilla, but made up for it by serving dumplings with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. i thought the crusts were a bit soggy. I think next time i will try pie crust cut into 8th's.
